newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens stocks hit new year high, end up 1.02pct.
newsitem.headline: Athens stocks hit new year high, end up 1.02pct.

text.p: Greek equities climbed again to a new 1997 high of 1,459.74 in early Thursday trade before settling at 1,456.95, up 1.02 percent, which is also a record year close.
Market analysts said the market is headed north, breaking away from critical resistance levels.

"Today's session gave evidence of the move away from the 1,450 resistance level which was a significant psychological barrier for quite a while," said Vasilios Kavalos, an analyst at Omega Securities.
Earlier today, Kappa Securities' managing director Spyros Bellos said the index will top 1,500 points next week.
Buying interest is spreading across the board from banking stocks to other sectors and analysts pointed out the rise in construction and select industrials.
"This rise in construction looks sustainable in view of rights issues scheduled for the coming months, yet investors should focus on sector leaders with clear prospects," Kavalos said.

The Athens general share index ended 1.02 percent or 14.76 points higher on Thursday, at 1,456.95, after opening at 1448.61. It had closed at 1,442.19 on Wednesdy. The session's high of 1,459.74 points was also a year high.
With the exception of small-caps which closed flat, all sub-indices ended higher. Banks and constructrion led the climb with rises of 1.40 and 1.44 percent respectively.
Turnover amounted to 13.4 billion drachmas on 4.7 million shares traded. Advancing stocks led decliners 144 to 78, with 23 shares unchanged on 245 traded.
Market analysts were quite happy about current levels of trading activity.
"Turnover is quite satisfactory bearing in mind we are ahead of a very long weekend," Kavalos said.
